quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: As a rider, how can you reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Do not look ahead for hazards.
Do not use turn signals because they can distract other drivers.
Make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, signal your intentions clearly, leave enough space between you and other vehicles, watch the road ahead, and spot hazards early. Always be ready to react to danger.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Blocks most of your side vision.
Lets you see enough to the sides for safe riding.
Can become unsafe for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Many people think helmets limit vision, but this is not true. A DOT-approved helmet allows you to see as much as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Because of this, you:

options.text: Do not need to wear bright clothing during the day.
Should wear bright clothing during the day.
Should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors when riding during the day to make yourself more noticeable.

questions.question: Can motorcyclists share a lane with other vehicles?

options.text: Yes, with cars.
Yes, when traffic is heavy.
No. Riders should use the full lane by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Riders should use the full lane by themselves.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to ride safely. Never share a lane with other vehicles.

questions.question: Your motorcycle has less grip for braking when:

options.text: The motorcycle is leaning.
The motorcycle is upright.
The pavement is dry.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a turn or curve, less grip is available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do so carefully.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance to four seconds?

options.text: When the road is wet or snowy.
When the road has multiple lanes.
When there is very little traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet or snowy.
questions.explanation: A three-second following distance is normally recommended. Increase it to four seconds when conditions make it harder to stop, such as rain or snow.

questions.question: While riding, where should your feet be?

options.text: On the gas tank.
Hanging loose.
On the footrests.

questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to help you stay balanced.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided highway ahead

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: When riding with a group, all riders should:

options.text: Check their mirrors often.
Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Not check mirrors because it can be distracting.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors regularly to watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: Avoid riding directly beside another vehicle because:

options.text: The driver may need your lane to pass another car.
You could be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little impact on whether or not other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it may affect whether or not other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it may affect whether or not other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps other drivers see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, you should:

options.text: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
Change lanes frequently.
Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you visible to other drivers. This reduces your risk of a collision. Always watch other drivers and be ready for their movements.

questions.question: It can be difficult to ride right after it starts raining because:

options.text: Some other drivers may not react quickly enough to the rain.
Pavement will be especially slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first falls. Oil from vehicles hasn't washed away yet, creating a slippery mixture with water.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Maintain an adequate space cushion.
Ride very slowly.
Ride the centerline.

questions.explanation: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Do this when following others, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Only ride in the left portion of the lane to better see around other vehicles ahead.
Ride closely to the vehicle in front of you to most effectively use their headlights.
Reduce your speed to increase your chances of avoiding an unexpected hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to increase your chances of avoiding an unexpected hazard.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and be flexible about where you position yourself in the lane.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is not a danger.
Can cause irreversible hearing damage.
Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Use ear protection when riding. It will protect you while still allowing you to hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: If vehicles are present on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually the best option?

options.text: Left
Right
Center

questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always bad. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions. If vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually safest.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always wear a jacket.
Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even in warm weather.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When using saddlebags to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
Put more weight in one bag than the other.
Put as much weight as possible in one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
questions.explanation: Load saddlebags with equal weight on both sides. Uneven weight causes the motorcycle to drift to one side.

questions.question: Keeping space between you and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles more easily.
You will be able to stop faster.
You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you more time to respond to hazards and more room to maneuver safely.
